stemMd: Residents of a town who volunteer at its river cleanup report greater satisfaction with local government than other residents. A councillor concludes that requiring every resident to volunteer will increase satisfaction with local government. Which is the clearest flaw?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The argument assumes satisfaction cannot be measured.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The argument uses a survey rather than a financial audit.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The argument assumes that the river is polluted.

options.label: D
options.textMd: People already satisfied with local government may be more likely to volunteer.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The argument fails to compare the town with a larger city.

explanationMd: The survey establishes an association, not the effect of volunteering. Satisfaction could precede and explain participation. A mandate would also change voluntary participation into compulsory participation, so the observed group is not a randomized intervention.

distractorRationale.a: It explicitly relies on measured reports.
distractorRationale.c: A cleanup can be useful without severe pollution; this does not identify the causal gap.
distractorRationale.e: A comparison city is not necessary to identify selection within this town.
distractorRationale.b: Satisfaction can appropriately be measured by survey.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Blind re-solve in the 5 November 2026 AI audit of this expansion (the review packet held no key, explanation or distractor notes; status "verified"; it checked for competing defensible answers and flagged none): Prior satisfaction may select volunteers; mandate does not reproduce that association.
